items.t: Said ensuring that only eligible citizens vote is the cornerstone of the democratic process.
items.q: The integrity of our elections is non-negotiable. Ensuring that only eligible citizens cast their votes is the cornerstone of our democratic process

items.t: Supports modernizing the SAVE system, saying it would remove delays and obstacles for state election offices.
items.q: By modernizing the SAVE system, we can eliminate unnecessary delays and obstacles that currently burden our state election offices.

items.t: Said voters' information should follow them when they move and that local election officials should have every available tool to maintain voter rolls.
items.q: When voters move, their information should follow them—and our local election officials deserve every available tool to keep the rolls clean, current, and transparent.

record.t: Was elected Missouri's 41st secretary of state.
record.q: Denny Hoskins was elected Missouri's 41st secretary of state in 2024.

record.office: Missouri Senate and Missouri House of Representatives
record.t: Served in the Missouri Senate and the Missouri House of Representatives before becoming secretary of state.
record.q: Previously, Hoskins served in the Missouri Senate and the Missouri House of Representatives.

record.t: Announced a new agreement with the State of Kansas on voter roll maintenance and voter registration records.
record.q: Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins announced a new agreement with the State of Kansas to improve voter roll maintenance and ensure more accurate, up-to-date voter registration records in both states.

record.t: Joined a coalition of state election officials in urging the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to reform the SAVE program.
record.q: Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, CPA, joined a coalition of state election officials in urging the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to implement significant reforms to the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program.

record.t: Said he would not approve a petition against the GOP-drawn congressional map and called the effort unconstitutional.
record.q: Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins on Tuesday said he would not approve a petition seeking to thwart the GOP-drawn map, calling the effort “unconstitutional.”

record.t: Said he would keep using the congressional districts redrawn last year, despite a U.S. Supreme Court decision leaving in place a state Supreme Court order to use the old districts.
record.q: Hoskins, a Republican, said Tuesday that he would keep using the congressional districts redrawn last year, despite a U.S. Supreme Court decision that left standing a state Supreme Court order requiring Missouri to use its old districts instead.

record.t: Requested an emergency stay from the U.S. Supreme Court, which Justice Brett Kavanaugh declined to grant, leaving the state Supreme Court injunction in place.
record.q: Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh declined to grant an emergency stay requested by Hoskins, leaving in place the injunction ordered by the state Supreme Court.

record.t: Was found in contempt by the Missouri Supreme Court for telling officials to use a new congressional map for the November election, and later the same day reversed course, which the court treated as purging the contempt.
record.q: The Missouri Supreme Court found Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins in contempt on Thursday for telling officials to use a new congressional map for the November election , but that Hoskins had “purged” himself of the contempt by reversing course later in the day.
